declared.title: The psychological health benefits of accepting negative emotions and thoughts: Laboratory, diary, and longitudinal evidence
declared.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
declared.foundIn: docs/design/review-science.md (dossier du pilote, 2026-11-22) ; titre de mémoire de la session

population: adults in 3 samples (N = 1,003, 156, 222); countries not given in the abstract

findings.text: People who habitually accept their negative emotions feel less negative emotion under daily stress, which accounts for better psychological health 6 months later

support.sentence: Finally, in a longitudinal design (Study 3, N = 222), acceptance predicted lower negative (but not positive) emotion experienced during daily stressors that, in turn, accounted for the link between acceptance and psychological health 6 months later.

findings.text: The benefit is for accepting one's feelings and thoughts, not for accepting one's situation

support.sentence: This link between acceptance and psychological health was unique to accepting mental experiences and was not observed for accepting situations.

findings.text: In the lab, people who habitually accept their emotions react with less negative emotion to a standard stressor

support.sentence: Next, in a laboratory study (Study 2, N = 156), habitual acceptance predicted lower negative (but not positive) emotional responses to a standardized stressor.

limits: habitual acceptance is measured, never manipulated: an association, not a cause
countries of the samples not given in the abstract (to read in the full text)
psychological health measured at 6 months without its baseline level (blind review, full text)
same network of authors as three other sources of this dossier (Iris Mauss): the evidence is not independent
